assessments.summary: Conditional on the structured transcription faithfully representing the visible theorem, the audit establishes the R0=0 specialization and exact 30-row equivalence, the input-only product marginalization of G and K, the extended-real inequalities V_Q(G,K) <= V(1/2;G,K) <= B(G,K), and the finite well-definedness of V_0(g,k) on its realizable domain. However, the declared all-or-nothing claim also requires a fail-closed, render-complete audit of the visible PDF, and the supplied checker does not validate actual Type1 glyph outlines or fully establish visual legibility and non-occlusion. With no counterexample to the pinned PDF, this unresolved source-fidelity obligation makes the claim indeterminate rather than invalid.
scopeQualifications: Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 is taken as a premise and is not independently re-proved.
The R0=0 specialization yields 26 inequality rows plus four side-condition rows; the chain-rule normalization used to compare them is valid.
Marginalization is established conditional on completeness of the audited term list: the system has no joint (G,K)-output term and no term conditioning one receiver output on another.
The convention sup(empty set)=-infinity makes the optimization inequalities meaningful for empty support-restricted feasible sets.

For Q0={0,1/2,1}, receiver-channel dependence is only through (J_Y(1/2),J_G(1/2),J_K(1/2),J_Z(1/2))=(c,g,k,c); feasibility is nonempty and zero-branch rate bounds give 0 <= V_0(g,k) <= 2 on the realizable (g,k)-domain.

The terminal attestation authenticates the pinned PDF and verifies its catalog, page structure, content operators, decoded glyph records, structured text comparison, 30 generated rows, and output-term whitelist, but it does not itself prove the theorem’s converse or execute the prose marginalization and optimization arguments; those arguments are separately mathematically sound conditional on transcription fidelity.
evidenceIssues: The checker inventories Type1 CharStrings and authenticates whole font programs by hard-coded digests, but it does not execute or geometrically validate the CharStrings.

Glyph names and ToUnicode mappings do not alone establish that the painted glyph outlines visibly represent the asserted characters; no independently auditable certificate connects the pinned font digests to the claimed outlines.

The geometry checks cover declared font bounding boxes, start positions, page containment, and limited same-baseline monotonicity, but do not establish non-occlusion or semantic legibility of the actual glyph outlines.
Matching a preselected geometry digest authenticates layout data but does not prove the omitted visual predicates required by the claim’s characterization of the audit as render-complete.
